Title: Magnum Bullarium Romanum, a Beato Leone Magno usque ad S.D.N. Benedictum XIV, Opus absolutissimum Laertii Cherubini: Tomus Secundus, a Pio IV ad Innocentium IX
Creator: Roman Catholic Church, papal constitutions of Pius IV, Pius V, Gregory XIII, Sixtus V, Gregory XIV and Innocent IX (collected by Laertius Cherubinus, expanded by Angelus Maria Cherubinus, Angelus a Lantusca and Joannes Paulus a Roma)
Publisher: Luxemburgi: Sumptibus Henrici-Alberti Gosse & Soc., "juxta exemplar Romae, ex typographia Reverendae Camerae Apostolicae"
Publication Date: 1727 (Internet Archive catalogue date; see Provenance note)
Rights: Public Domain (published in the 1720s-1750s; public domain by date)
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item gri_33125011258403 (volume 02 of the 1727 Luxembourg Magnum bullarium Romanum; contributor Getty Research Institute), file gri_33125011258403_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: none (the item carries no possible-copyright-status, licence or access-restriction field; it downloads openly).
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged, no long-s normalisation needed (the OCR already renders long s as f and contains no long-s characters, 0 replaced). The Internet Archive catalogue dates this set 1727. The title page in the OCR names Benedict XIV (pope 1740-1758) and its imprint year is garbled ("M OD Gc"), so the year is the catalogue's, not read from the page; either date falls well before 1930. Public domain by the project's date rule (published 1930 or earlier).
Content note: One volume of the Luxembourg Magnum bullarium Romanum, Tomus Secundus, "A Pio IV ad Innocentium IX" (Pius IV, Pius V, Gregory XIII, Sixtus V, Gregory XIV, Innocent IX), with the editors' rubrics, summaries and scholia. Latin. It prints Sixtus V's constitution 74, Immensa aeterni Dei (1588), founding the fifteen cardinalitial Congregations of the Roman Curia ("LXXIV. Institutio quindecim Congregationum"). The OCR is a clean Latin print with ordinary long-s-as-f spellings ("Ecclefia"); sampled at five points (10/30/50/70/90 percent) and readable at each. Whole-file share of word-shaped tokens: 0.72. The volume is the editors' collection with their own scholia; the papal constitutions are the primary text. No public-domain English translation of these constitutions was found.
